filename: Spatio-Temporal Machine Learning Models for Emulation of Global Atmospheric Composition.pdf
title: Spatio-Temporal Machine Learning Models for Emulation of Global Atmospheric Composition
venue: Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning: workshop at NeurIPS 2024
parameterization_target: surface-level biomass burning black carbon concentration
testbed_rationale: The simulation dataset generated using NASA GISS ModelE3 and the model code are not publicly linked or documented with an open data access URL.
pain_points: Aerosol concentrations vary over multiple orders of magnitude between source and remote regions, leading standard loss functions (MSE/MAE) to heavily misestimate low concentrations or underrepresent extreme high peaks.
Underestimation of peak concentration events (e.g., during Northern Hemisphere wildfire seasons and extreme events >630e-11 kg/kg_air).
High GPU memory (VRAM) consumption when integrating self-attention mechanisms or moving to 3D vertical aerosol emulation.
Boundary conditioning required special cyclic padding across longitudes and reflective padding across poles.
extraction_notes: The paper trains an offline ConvLSTM to emulate advective tracer transport at surface pressure levels for biomass burning black carbon. Online coupling into NASA GISS-E2.1 via FTorch is discussed as planned future work.
